clause.text: 1 PURPOSE OF THE AGREEMENT
clause.heading: 1 PURPOSE OF THE AGREEMENT

reviews.rationale: The clause only states a generic purpose heading and does not contain any substantive terms that could create liability, third‑party rights, or other contractual risks. It aligns with the playbook’s expectation that purpose statements be minimal and does not conflict with any of the listed positions.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement is for the benefit of the parties and their permitted successors and assigns only. No other person has any right to enforce any of its terms.

clause.text: 1.1 The purpose of this content distribution Agreement (hereinafter "Agreement") is to set forth the terms and conditions under which plan_b may use the Content ("Content" as set forth in APPENDIX 2) owned or licensed by LICENSOR for a commercial distribution to plan_b's End Users in the territory ("Territory" as set forth in APPENDIX 2).
clause.heading: 1.1 The purpose of this content distribution Agreement (hereinafter "Agreement") is to set forth the terms and conditions under which plan_b may use the Content ("Content" as set forth in APPENDIX 2) owned or licensed by LICENSOR for a commercial distribution to plan_b's End Users in the territory ("Territory" as set forth in APPENDIX 2).

reviews.rationale: The clause only states the purpose and scope of the content distribution but does not address ownership of the intellectual property or the scope and duration of the licence, which are required by the company's playbook. Specifically, the playbook requires a clause that the parties shall not jointly own any intellectual property ([ip-no-joint-ownership]) and that no licence is perpetual, irrevocable, or unlimited ([licence-not-perpetual]). The absence of these provisions creates a moderate risk that the agreement could be interpreted as granting joint ownership or an overly broad licence.

citations.excerpt: The parties shall not jointly own any intellectual property under this Agreement. Any jointly developed work product shall be owned by the party that contributed the underlying background intellectual property, with a licence granted to the other party as set out in this Agreement.

No licence granted under this Agreement is perpetual, irrevocable, or unlimited in volume, territory or field of use. Each licence is co-terminous with this Agreement and bounded by the metrics stated in the applicable Order Form.

clause.text: 1.2 End User means any third Party receiving Content on a mobile device for a payment in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement for their own private and non- commercial use.
clause.heading: 1.2 End User means any third Party receiving Content on a mobile device for a payment in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement for their own private and non- commercial use.

reviews.rationale: The clause merely defines "End User" as a third party receiving content for private, non‑commercial use. It does not create rights for third parties, impose pricing obligations, or affect intellectual property. This aligns with the playbook position that the agreement is for the benefit of the parties only and does not create third‑party beneficiary rights.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement is for the benefit of the parties and their permitted successors and assigns only. No other person has any right to enforce any of its terms.

clause.text: 2 OBLIGATIONS OF LICENSOR
clause.heading: 2 OBLIGATIONS OF LICENSOR

reviews.rationale: The clause only provides a heading without any substantive obligations, so it does not impose any specific duties or liabilities on the licensor. This lack of detail presents minimal contractual risk. The playbook recommends bounding obligations, as illustrated in the post-termination provision that limits duties to those that expressly survive.

citations.excerpt: On termination or expiry, each party's obligations cease except for those that expressly survive.

clause.text: 2.1 LICENSOR shall make a first delivery of Content to plan_b within 14 days after the signing of this Agreement unless separately agreed between the Parties.
clause.heading: 2.1 LICENSOR shall make a first delivery of Content to plan_b within 14 days after the signing of this Agreement unless separately agreed between the Parties.

reviews.rationale: The clause imposes a delivery deadline of 14 days, which if missed could constitute a material breach. The playbook’s termination‑for‑cause‑cure provision states that a party may terminate for cause if the other party materially breaches and fails to cure within thirty (30) days after notice, indicating that timely performance is a critical contractual obligation.

citations.excerpt: Either party may terminate this Agreement for cause if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure that breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing the breach in reasonable detail.

clause.text: 2.2 LICENSOR shall deliver Content according to the specifications (for example formats, file sizes) set by plan_b or to be agreed between the Parties in writing.
clause.heading: 2.2 LICENSOR shall deliver Content according to the specifications (for example formats, file sizes) set by plan_b or to be agreed between the Parties in writing.

reviews.rationale: The clause merely requires the licensor to deliver content according to specifications set by plan_b or agreed in writing. This does not create joint ownership of intellectual property, impose indemnity obligations, or affect confidentiality or payment terms. Therefore it does not conflict with any of the playbook positions and presents minimal contractual risk.

citations.excerpt: The parties shall not jointly own any intellectual property under this Agreement.

clause.text: 2.3 LICENSOR grants plan_b for the term of this Agreement the right to produce, market and distribute Content to End Users (in the territory specified in appendix 2) through its own and its partner's platform.
clause.heading: 2.3 LICENSOR grants plan_b for the term of this Agreement the right to produce, market and distribute Content to End Users (in the territory specified in appendix 2) through its own and its partner's platform.

reviews.rationale: The clause grants Plan_B a broad right to produce, market and distribute content without limitations, which conflicts with the playbook position that licences must be limited, non-transferable and non-sublicensable (licence-scope-limited) and must not be perpetual, irrevocable or unlimited in scope (licence-not-perpetual). These deviations create significant IP risk.

citations.excerpt: non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable licence
No licence granted under this Agreement is perpetual, irrevocable, or unlimited

clause.text:
3 OBLIGATIONS OF PLAN_B

 3.1 plan_b will distribute Content to End Users in the Territory through its distribution channels.

 3.2 plan_b shall use reasonable commercial efforts to market and stimulate interest in the Content with its customers.

 3.3 plan_b shall provide LICENSOR with a detailed written record, which includes the number of End User downloads and each distribution channel. Such report shall be provided to LICENSOR in electronic format within 6 weeks of the end of a quarter.
clause.heading: 3 OBLIGATIONS OF PLAN_B

reviews.rationale: The clause requires plan_b to provide a detailed download report within 6 weeks of quarter end. None of the retrieved playbook positions address reporting timelines or create a conflict with this requirement. Therefore, the clause aligns with the playbook and presents no identified risk.

clause.text:
3.4 LICENSOR shall have the right to use a certified public accountant to inspect and audit all the related records and books of plan_b to ensure plan_b's compliance with the terms of this Agreement. In the event that any such audit reveals that plan_b has underpaid fees to the value of ten (10) percent or more of the total amount of payments for the period covered by the audit, plan_b shall bear the cost of the audit and shall in any event immediately pay to LICENSOR

Source: DATA CALL TECHNOLOGIES, SB-2/A, 9/18/2006

 the full value of the underpaid or under-reported fees. Such audits shall normally be conducted during normal business hours at plan_b's premises.
clause.heading: 3.4 LICENSOR shall have the right to use a certified public accountant to inspect and audit all the related records and books of plan_b to ensure plan_b's compliance with the terms of this Agreement. In the event that any such audit reveals that plan_b has underpaid fees to the value of ten (10) percent or more of the total amount of payments for the period covered by the audit, plan_b shall bear the cost of the audit and shall in any event immediately pay to LICENSOR

reviews.rationale: The clause gives LICENSOR unrestricted audit rights and requires plan_b to bear all audit costs, even when the audit does not reveal an underpayment. This contrasts with the playbook position which limits audits to at most twice per year, requires prior notice, and places the cost on the audited party only if an underpayment greater than five percent is found. The unrestricted scope and cost allocation increase the company's exposure, resulting in a high risk assessment.

citations.excerpt: A party may audit the other party's records relevant to this Agreement no more than twice in any twelve (12) month period, on fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and subject to the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement. The audited party bears the cost only if the audit reveals an underpayment of more than five percent (5%).

reviews.suggested_fallback: A party may audit the other party's records relevant to this Agreement no more than twice in any twelve (12) month period, on fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and subject to the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement. The audited party bears the cost only if the audit reveals an underpayment of more than five percent (5%).

clause.text:
4 REVENUES

 4.1 plan_b shall pay LICENSOR a share of its revenues as set forth in APPENDIX 2 ("REVENUES").
clause.heading: 4 REVENUES

reviews.rationale: The clause requires payment of a revenue share but does not define how the revenue share is calculated, capped, or audited. This omission conflicts with the playbook position [revenue-share-defined] which mandates that any revenue or profit share be calculated on a specified basis and within a defined timeframe. Without such definition, the clause leaves the licensor exposed to ambiguous payment terms and potential disputes, constituting a high risk.

citations.excerpt: Any revenue or profit share payable under this Agreement shall be calculated on gross revenue actually received, at the percentage stated in the Order Form, and shall be payable within forty-five (45) days of the end of each calendar quarter together with a statement showing the calculation.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Any revenue or profit share payable under this Agreement shall be calculated on gross revenue actually received, at the percentage stated in the Order Form, and shall be payable within forty-five (45) days of the end of each calendar quarter together with a statement showing the calculation.

clause.text: 4.2 All shares are net, plus the respective applying value added tax (if applicable).
clause.heading: 4.2 All shares are net, plus the respective applying value added tax (if applicable).

reviews.rationale: The clause states that shares are calculated on a net basis plus any applicable value added tax. This conflicts with the playbook's revenue‑share position, which requires that revenue or profit share be calculated on net revenue without additional tax (Preferred wording). Adding VAT increases the amount payable beyond the net revenue defined in the playbook, creating a material deviation and financial risk.

citations.excerpt: Any revenue or profit share payable under this Agreement shall be calculated on net revenue actually received, at the percentage stated in the Order Form, and shall be payable within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar quarter together with a statement showing the calculation.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Any revenue or profit share payable under this Agreement shall be calculated on net revenue actually received, at the percentage stated in the Order Form, and shall be payable within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar quarter together with a statement showing the calculation.

clause.text: 5 INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS
clause.heading: 5 INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS

reviews.rationale: The clause only restates the heading for intellectual property rights without specifying any terms that conflict with the playbook. The playbook requires each party to retain its background IP and prohibits joint ownership unless expressly licensed. Since the clause provides no substantive language, it aligns with the preferred position that each party retains its own IP and does not create joint ownership or transfer rights, posing minimal risk.

citations.excerpt: Each party retains all right, title and interest in the intellectual property it owned before this Agreement or develops independently of it. Nothing in this Agreement transfers ownership of a party's intellectual property to the other party.

The parties shall not jointly own any intellectual property under this Agreement. Any jointly developed work product shall be owned by the party that contributed the underlying background intellectual property, with a licence granted to the other party as set out in this Agreement.

clause.text: 5.1 LICENSOR is the owner of all intellectual property rights, including without limitation, any and all patents, utility models, trade marks, rights in designs, trade, business or domain names, know-how, rights in databases and copyrights, rights in inventions, ideas, concepts, trade secrets and confidential information which have to be given to fulfill this contract.
clause.heading: 5.1 LICENSOR is the owner of all intellectual property rights, including without limitation, any and all patents, utility models, trade marks, rights in designs, trade, business or domain names, know-how, rights in databases and copyrights, rights in inventions, ideas, concepts, trade secrets and confidential information which have to be given to fulfill this contract.

reviews.rationale: The clause transfers all intellectual property rights to the Licensor, which directly contradicts the playbook positions that require each party to retain its own background IP and prohibit joint ownership. The playbook position "ip-each-party-keeps-its-own" states that "Each party retains all right, title and interest in the intellectual property it owned before this Agreement or develops independently of it. Nothing in this Agreement transfers ownership of a party's intellectual property to the other party." Additionally, the "ip-no-joint-ownership" position mandates that "The parties shall not jointly own any intellectual property under this Agreement." Therefore, the clause poses a high risk of violating the company's IP ownership policy.

citations.excerpt: Each party retains all right, title and interest in the intellectual property it owned before this Agreement or develops independently of it. Nothing in this Agreement transfers ownership of a party's intellectual property to the other party.

The parties shall not jointly own any intellectual property under this Agreement. Any jointly developed work product shall be owned by the party that contributed the underlying background intellectual property, with a licence granted to the other party as set out in this Agreement.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Each party retains all right, title and interest in the intellectual property it owned before this Agreement or develops independently of it. Nothing in this Agreement transfers ownership of a party's intellectual property to the other party.

clause.text: 5.2 In the alternative, if LICENSOR is not the sole and exclusive owner of all of the foregoing intellectual property rights to the Content, LICENSOR has been granted by the owner or rightful sub-licensee of the intellectual property of the Content the right to grant the rights provided by LICENSOR to plan_b under this Agreement.
clause.heading: 5.2 In the alternative, if LICENSOR is not the sole and exclusive owner of all of the foregoing intellectual property rights to the Content, LICENSOR has been granted by the owner or rightful sub-licensee of the intellectual property of the Content the right to grant the rights provided by LICENSOR to plan_b under this Agreement.

reviews.rationale: The clause permits the licensor to grant rights to the content even when the licensor is not the sole and exclusive owner, relying on sub‑licensing from a third party. This conflicts with the playbook positions that prohibit joint ownership of intellectual property (ip-no-joint-ownership) and require each party to retain its own background IP without transferring ownership (ip-each-party-keeps-its-own). Allowing rights to be granted by a non‑owner creates uncertainty about ownership and licensing rights, increasing the risk of IP disputes and liability.

citations.excerpt: The parties shall not jointly own any intellectual property under this Agreement.
Each party retains all right, title and interest in the intellectual property it owned before this Agreement or develops independently of it.

clause.text: 5.3 LICENSOR grants to plan_b a license to produce, use, distribute, promote and publicly display the Content in any possible way for distribution and marketing purposes. Additionally, Licensee shall have the right to use the trademarks, trade names, or logos relating to Content (the "TRADEMARKS").
clause.heading: 5.3 LICENSOR grants to plan_b a license to produce, use, distribute, promote and publicly display the Content in any possible way for distribution and marketing purposes. Additionally, Licensee shall have the right to use the trademarks, trade names, or logos relating to Content (the "TRADEMARKS").

reviews.rationale: The clause provides a broad, unrestricted licence to "produce, use, distribute, promote and publicly display the Content in any possible way for distribution and marketing purposes" and additionally permits use of trademarks, trade names, or logos. This exceeds the limited, non‑transferable licence scope required by the playbook, which restricts use to internal business purposes and sets clear limits on sublicensing. The mismatch creates significant risk of over‑granting IP rights.

citations.excerpt: Supplier grants Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable licence to use the Services during the Term solely for Customer's internal business purposes. The licence terminates automatically on expiry or termination of this Agreement.

The licence terminates automatically on expiry or termination of this Agreement.

clause.text: 5.4 LICENSOR warrants that Content does not infringe an intellectual property right enforceable in the agreed country of delivery or use. LICENSOR indemnifies and holds harmless plan_b against all claims that Content infringes any of the above mentioned rights of a third Party. LICENSOR shall pay all damages awarded in a trial to a third Party.
clause.heading: 5.4 LICENSOR warrants that Content does not infringe an intellectual property right enforceable in the agreed country of delivery or use. LICENSOR indemnifies and holds harmless plan_b against all claims that Content infringes any of the above mentioned rights of a third Party. LICENSOR shall pay all damages awarded in a trial to a third Party.

reviews.rationale: The clause obligates the Licensor to indemnify and hold harmless the customer and to pay damages, but it does not include a duty to defend the customer against third‑party IP infringement claims. The playbook's preferred language requires both defense and indemnification, so the clause is missing a key element and therefore carries medium risk.

citations.excerpt: Supplier shall defend and indemnify Customer against any third-party claim alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe that third party's intellectual property rights, and shall pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.

clause.text: 6 CONFIDENTIALITY
clause.heading: 6 CONFIDENTIALITY

reviews.rationale: The clause provides only a heading with no substantive confidentiality obligations. The playbook requires explicit confidentiality obligations, including duration (confidentiality-term) and mutual duties with standard exclusions (confidentiality-mutual). Because the clause omits these required terms, it deviates significantly from the preferred language, creating high contractual risk.

citations.excerpt: The confidentiality obligations in this Agreement survive for three (3) years after termination or expiry, and indefinitely with respect to trade secrets for so long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.

Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information confidential, use it only to perform this Agreement, and protect it with at least the care it uses for its own confidential information. These obligations do not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving party, was already known to it, or is independently developed by it.

clause.text:
6.1 Each Party shall keep in confidence all material and information, including without limitation Content, received from the other Party and marked as confidential or which should be understood to be confidential, and may not use such material or information for any other purposes than those set forth in this Agreement. The confidentiality obligation shall, however, not be applied to material and information, which as shown by the receiving Party,

 6.1.1 is generally available or otherwise public; or

 6.1.2 the receiving Party has received from a third party without any obligation of confidentiality; or

 6.1.3 was in the possession of the receiving Party prior to receipt of the same from the other Party without any obligation of confidentiality related thereto; or

 6.1.4 the receiving party has independently developed without using material or information received from the other Party.
clause.heading: 6.1 Each Party shall keep in confidence all material and information, including without limitation Content, received from the other Party and marked as confidential or which should be understood to be confidential, and may not use such material or information for any other purposes than those set forth in this Agreement. The confidentiality obligation shall, however, not be applied to material and information, which as shown by the receiving Party,

reviews.rationale: The clause requires each party to keep confidential information confidential and limits use to the agreement, which aligns with the playbook's mutual confidentiality position. However, it omits the playbook's required protection standard: "protect it with at least the care it uses for its own confidential information." This missing language weakens the obligation and therefore represents a higher risk.

citations.excerpt: Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information confidential, use it only to perform this Agreement, and protect it with at least the care it uses for its own confidential information.

clause.text: 6.2 Each Party shall promptly upon termination of this Agreement or when the Party no longer needs the material or information in question for the purpose stated in this Agreement cease using confidential material and information received from the other Party and, unless the Parties separately agree on destruction of such material, return the material in question (including all copies thereof).
clause.heading: 6.2 Each Party shall promptly upon termination of this Agreement or when the Party no longer needs the material or information in question for the purpose stated in this Agreement cease using confidential material and information received from the other Party and, unless the Parties separately agree on destruction of such material, return the material in question (including all copies thereof).

reviews.rationale: The clause only obliges the parties to cease using and return confidential material upon termination, but it does not include the protective standard of using "at least the care it uses for its own confidential information" nor the standard exclusions for public, already known, or independently developed information. Because these required elements are absent, the risk is high as indicated by the playbook.

citations.excerpt: Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information confidential, use it only to perform this Agreement, and protect it with at least the care it uses for its own confidential information. These obligations do not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving party, was already known to it, or is independently developed by it.

clause.text: 6.3 The rights and responsibilities under this section shall survive any termination or cancellation of this Agreement for 2 years.
clause.heading: 6.3 The rights and responsibilities under this section shall survive any termination or cancellation of this Agreement for 2 years.

reviews.rationale: The clause requires that rights survive for 2 years after termination. The playbook's confidentiality position states a preferred survival period of three (3) years, which is longer than the clause's 2-year period. Since the clause's survival term is shorter than the preferred standard, it does not exceed the playbook's expectations and therefore presents low risk.

citations.excerpt: The confidentiality obligations in this Agreement survive for three (3) years after termination or expiry, and indefinitely with respect to trade secrets for so long as they remain trade secrets under applicable law.

clause.text:
7 TERM OF THE AGREEMENT AND TERMINATION

Source: DATA CALL TECHNOLOGIES, SB-2/A, 9/18/2006
clause.heading: 7 TERM OF THE AGREEMENT AND TERMINATION

reviews.rationale: The clause provides only a heading and lacks any substantive termination or renewal language. The playbook specifies that renewal must be opt‑in and not automatic (renewal‑opt‑in). Because the clause omits this required provision, the risk is elevated to medium.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement expires at the end of the Initial Term and shall renew only if both parties agree in writing to renew it. Any renewal term shall not exceed twelve (12) months.

clause.text: 7.1 Unless otherwise stated in the Appendix the term of this letter Agreement shall continue for twenty-four (24) months with the effective date unless terminated sooner or extended pursuant to the terms hereof ("Initial Term"). The Initial Term shall automatically be extended for an additional period of half a year unless either party provides the other party with written notification of termination of the letter Agreement at least 60 days prior to end of such period.
clause.heading: 7.1 Unless otherwise stated in the Appendix the term of this letter Agreement shall continue for twenty-four (24) months with the effective date unless terminated sooner or extended pursuant to the terms hereof ("Initial Term"). The Initial Term shall automatically be extended for an additional period of half a year unless either party provides the other party with written notification of termination of the letter Agreement at least 60 days prior to end of such period.

reviews.rationale: The clause provides an automatic six‑month extension of the Initial Term unless notice is given, which directly conflicts with the playbook’s renewal‑opt‑in position that requires renewal only with written agreement of both parties. This mismatch creates a medium‑risk situation as the playbook specifies a medium risk when renewal provisions are not aligned with the opt‑in principle.

citations.excerpt: Renewal is opt-in, not automatic

clause.text: 7.2 Either Party shall be entitled to cancel this Agreement if the other Party is materially in breach of the terms of this Agreement. If the breach of contract is capable of being remedied, this Agreement can be cancelled only provided that the Party in breach has not rectified its breach within thirty (30) days of the written notice by the other Party.
clause.heading: 7.2 Either Party shall be entitled to cancel this Agreement if the other Party is materially in breach of the terms of this Agreement. If the breach of contract is capable of being remedied, this Agreement can be cancelled only provided that the Party in breach has not rectified its breach within thirty (30) days of the written notice by the other Party.

reviews.rationale: The clause aligns with the playbook’s preferred termination‑for‑cause language, allowing either party to terminate for a material breach if not cured within thirty (30) days after written notice. This matches the Preferred text of the termination‑for‑cause‑cure position, so it presents no deviation from the company’s standard.

citations.excerpt: Either party may terminate this Agreement for cause if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure that breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing the breach in reasonable detail.

clause.text: 7.3 Either Party may cancel this Agreement already prior to the date of its fulfillment, if it becomes evident that the other Party will commit a breach of contract entitling to cancellation of this Agreement.
clause.heading: 7.3 Either Party may cancel this Agreement already prior to the date of its fulfillment, if it becomes evident that the other Party will commit a breach of contract entitling to cancellation of this Agreement.

reviews.rationale: The clause allows either party to cancel the agreement upon merely becoming aware of a potential breach, without requiring a cure period or written notice. This deviates from the playbook's termination‑for‑cause‑cure position, which mandates a thirty‑day (preferred) or forty‑five‑day (fallback) cure period after written notice describing the breach. The lack of a cure window increases exposure to premature termination and potential disputes, thus representing a high risk.

citations.excerpt: Either party may terminate this Agreement for cause if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure that breach within forty-five (45) days after receiving written notice describing the breach in reasonable detail.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Either party may terminate this Agreement for cause if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure that breach within forty-five (45) days after receiving written notice describing the breach in reasonable detail.

clause.text: 7.4 Upon termination or cancellation of this Agreement plan_b shall cease to use Content for any purpose and delete Content from any files and data storage.
clause.heading: 7.4 Upon termination or cancellation of this Agreement plan_b shall cease to use Content for any purpose and delete Content from any files and data storage.

reviews.rationale: The clause requires the party to cease using and delete Content upon termination, which aligns with the playbook's requirement to return or delete the other party's data. However, the playbook also mandates providing reasonable transition assistance for up to sixty (60) days and specifies that deletion should be done on request. The clause omits any transition assistance period and the conditional "on request" language, creating a gap that could leave the company without needed support during wind‑down. This partial compliance raises a moderate risk.

citations.excerpt: On termination or expiry, each party's obligations cease except for those that expressly survive. Supplier shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to sixty (60) days at its then-current rates, and shall return or delete the other party's data on request.

clause.text: 7.5 After termination of this contract, there shall be a sell-off period (defined in APPENDIX 2) following the date of termination of this contract.
clause.heading: 7.5 After termination of this contract, there shall be a sell-off period (defined in APPENDIX 2) following the date of termination of this contract.

reviews.rationale: The clause introduces a post‑termination sell‑off period, creating an additional obligation that is not addressed in the company’s playbook. The playbook explicitly states that no extra sums or obligations, such as liquidated damages or termination fees, may be imposed on termination (liquidated-damages‑none). Introducing a sell‑off period therefore conflicts with the principle that termination should not create further liabilities, raising the risk to high.

citations.excerpt: Neither party shall owe liquidated damages, a termination fee, or any other pre‑agreed sum on termination or expiry of this Agreement; each party's remedy for breach is limited to its actual proven damages, subject to the limitations of liability in this Agreement.

clause.text: 8 MISCELLANEOUS
clause.heading: 8 MISCELLANEOUS

reviews.rationale: The clause is a generic heading with no substantive terms, posing minimal contractual risk. It aligns with standard practice and does not introduce obligations or rights that conflict with the playbook.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement is for the benefit of the parties and their permitted successors and assigns only. No other person has any right to enforce any of its terms.

clause.heading: 8.1 The Parties acknowledge that they act as independent contractors and this Agreement does not constitute any partnership, joint venture, agency relationship or other independent legal entity separate from the Parties.

This aligns with the playbook's approach of limiting the agreement to the parties and their permitted successors and assigns, confirming that no additional entities gain rights or responsibilities beyond those expressly defined. citations.excerpt: This Agreement is for the benefit of the parties and their permitted successors and assigns only. No other person has any right to enforce any of its terms.

clause.text: 8.2 Neither Party shall assign or transfer to any third party, without the prior written consent of the other Party, this Agreement or any rights granted herein.
clause.heading: 8.2 Neither Party shall assign or transfer to any third party, without the prior written consent of the other Party, this Agreement or any rights granted herein.

reviews.rationale: The clause restricts assignment without consent, matching the playbook's assignment position that allows assignment only with prior written consent and provides specific exceptions. citations.excerpt: Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except that either party may assign it in its entirety, on notice and without consent, to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets.

clause.heading: 8.3 Any amendments to this Agreement shall be in writing and shall have no effect before signed by the duly authorized representatives of the Parties.

clause.text: 8.4 All payments will be made to Licensor in United States dollars.
clause.heading: 8.4 All payments will be made to Licensor in United States dollars.

clause.text: 9 SEVERABILITY
clause.heading: 9 SEVERABILITY

reviews.rationale: The clause is a standard severability provision which does not conflict with any of the company's playbook positions.
